name: fittings
description: Fittings recognised by SHAPE in DXF geometry (vpt/fittings.py, vpt/dxf_symbols.py, tools/recognise_fittings.py). Plain lines, arcs, circles and polylines on the fitting layers are grouped into symbols and classified by the rules below; rooms are those of presets/plan_extract.json.
status: STARTING VALUES - confirm. Written for the toolkit's synthetic flat and typical sizes of sanitary and kitchen symbols, not measured on a real drawing. Change them here; the tool re-runs. Nothing is guessed: a symbol no rule matches is 'unrecognised', one that two rules match is 'ambiguous'; both are listed.
fitting_layers_note: Base layer names (the part after <storey>_<nn>_[Abbruch_|Neubau_]). Furniture layers are left out on purpose: a furniture outline would be 'unrecognised' and flagged.

shape_rules.exclude_status_note: Layers with this status prefix (demolished content) are segmented and classified too, but reported as 'demolished' and left out of every count and check. The same status is left out of the room labels, outlines and walls used for assigning rooms (presets/plan_extract.json).
shape_rules.segmentation_note: Two primitives belong to one symbol when their lines come within join_tol_m (5 mm) of each other, or when one lies inside the convex hull of the other and that other is at most contain_max_m long (a drain circle inside a basin; not every item inside a room-sized outline). Groups whose oriented box is shorter than min_symbol_m on its long side are counted as 'fragments', not symbols. Arcs and curves are flattened with flatten_m. A face of the linework (a closed loop) counts when its area is at least min_face_m2.
shape_rules.features_note: Per symbol: w_m >= d_m (minimum-area rectangle, metres), aspect = w/d, closed_loops (faces of the linework), circles / circle radii (CIRCLE entities), small_circles (radius <= small_circle_max_r_m: drain or tap), curved_primitives (primitives with any arc or curved piece, hatches left out), arc_share (length of arcs and curves / all line length, hatches left out), diagonal_lines (straight pieces from one corner of the rectangle to the opposite one, within diagonal_corner_tol_frac of the diagonal), text_cue (a text whose insertion point lies inside the rectangle, grown by text_tol_m, matches the rule's regex; texts are only cues, never reported).
shape_rules.assignment_note: Room of a symbol: plan_extract.assign at its centre: (a) the smallest closed room outline around it that holds a room label, else (b) the nearest room label within label_max_dist_m whose straight line to the centre crosses no wall segment, else no room (flagged by F2).

rules.note: Pan with a rounded front (an arc or ellipse) and a tank: at least three closed loops (tank, pan outline, bowl); no circle at all (a drain circle is a basin; several circles of this size are a cooktop).
Basin with a rounded bowl and either a small drain circle or just two loops (outline and bowl), so it cannot be a WC (three loops).
Bath: an outline with an inner outline (at least two closed loops).
Shower tray, roughly square, drawn with its diagonals or a drain circle.
Kitchen sink: a rectangular outline with a rectangular inner basin, no curves.
One hotplate: a single circle. A hob of four plates is four of these.
Kitchen counter: one long plain rectangle. On a furniture layer a plain rectangle of this size (a wardrobe) would match too: keep furniture layers out of fitting_layers.
Washing machine, roughly square, labelled WM (a text inside the symbol) or drawn with its drum.

shape_rules.rules_note: A rule matches when w_m and d_m are inside its ranges, aspect <= max_aspect (if given), every condition under 'all' holds and at least one under 'any' holds (if given). A condition is {feature, min, max} on a feature above; 'circles' may carry r_m [lo, hi] to count only circles of that radius; 'text_cue' carries a regex.
